summary: Game crashes after creating/entering a Debug Type world
description: The game crashed whilst ticking player 1.16.2-pre2: [^crash-2020-08-05_11.26.54-server.txt] Description: Ticking player java.lang.IllegalStateException: Unregistered biome at bw.b(SourceFile:88) at bw$$Lambda$4540/1295484091.get(Unknown Source) at java.util.Optional.orElseThrow(Optional.java:290) at bw.a(SourceFile:88) at bw.a(SourceFile:68) at bx$a.a(SourceFile:55) at bx.a(SourceFile:31) at bx$$Lambda$4537/457642732.test(Unknown Source) at ck.a(SourceFile:62) at bx.a(SourceFile:31) at aah.v_(SourceFile:484) at aay.b(SourceFile:207) at nd.a(SourceFile:234) at aax.c(SourceFile:173) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.b(SourceFile:881) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:810) at emy.a(SourceFile:92) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.w(SourceFile:669) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:254) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer$$Lambda$4097/78048568.run(Unknown Source) at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft version 1.16.2‑pre2.  
2. From the main menu select **Singleplayer** → **Create New World**.  
3. Click **More World Options**, set **World Type** to **Debug**, and confirm the selection.  
4. Click **Create New World** to generate and load the Debug world.  
5. Wait a few seconds for the world to finish loading.  
6. Observe that the game crashes while ticking the player.
Observed Behavior:
- In Minecraft **Java Edition 1.16.2‑pre2**, selecting the **Debug** world type (the “look‑but‑don’t‑touch” world) and either **creating a new world** with that type or **loading an existing Debug world** causes the server to crash **while the first player is being ticked**.  
- The crash is triggered during the player‑tick phase and results in an **`java.lang.IllegalStateException: Unregistered biome`**. The relevant stack trace (excerpt from the generated `crash‑reports/*.txt`) is:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Unregistered biome
    at bw.b(SourceFile:88)
    at bw$$Lambda$4540/1295484091.get(Unknown Source)
    at java.util.Optional.orElseThrow(Optional.java:290)
    at bw.a(SourceFile:88)
    at bw.a(SourceFile:68)
    at bx$a.a(SourceFile:55)
    at bx.a(SourceFile:31)
    …
    at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.b(SourceFile:881)
    at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:810)
    at emy.a(SourceFile:92)
    at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.w(SourceFile:669)
    at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:254)
    at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer$$Lambda$4097/78048568.run(Unknown Source)
    at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745)
```

- The exception originates from the biome‑lookup code (`bw.*` classes) which attempts to resolve a biome that is **not registered** in the Debug world’s biome registry. Because the Debug world is intended to be a read‑only “spectator‑only” environment with a fixed biome (Plains), the missing registration should never be consulted; however, the player‑tick logic still queries the biome for the player’s current position, causing the illegal state.  

- As a result, the **entire server process terminates**:

  * The server console prints the full stack trace and “**Crash report saved to** …/crash‑reports/crash‑2020‑08‑05_11.26.54-server.txt”.  
  * All connected players are disconnected with no further world interaction possible.  
  * No world data is corrupted, but the crash prevents any further play in Debug worlds until the bug is fixed.  

- This behaviour is **reproducible** on every launch of a Debug world in the specified version, regardless of the player’s gamemode, location, or whether the world is newly generated or loaded from disk
Expected Behavior: When a Debug Type world is created and entered, the server should load the world without error, register all default biomes (including the Plains biome), and continue ticking the player normally. The player’s position, inventory and game state should update each tick without triggering an exception, allowing normal gameplay and observation of the debug world’s block‑state visualization.
